name: Areli
overview: Areli was a male member of the tribe of Gad, identified explicitly as the son of Gad. He is noted in the biblical record as part of the descendants of Israel who went to Egypt, linking him to the foundational narrative of the Israelites' sojourn in Egypt. Areli's lineage is associated with the Arelite clan mentioned in the book of Numbers, indicating his descendants formed a recognized family group within the tribe of Gad.
namesAndTitles: The name Areli appears as a proper name in Scripture without a given meaning or divine origin noted. It is recorded plainly in Genesis 46:16, serving primarily as an identifier for this individual within the genealogical records.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture clearly records Areli as the son of Gad, establishing his direct paternal relationship. Beyond this explicit connection, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text concerning Areli.
scriptureSignificance: Areli's significance lies in his place within the genealogical and tribal history of Israel. As a son of Gad, he represents one of the ancestral figures whose family migrated to Egypt, a critical event in God's providential plan for His people. The mention of the Arelites in Numbers as descendants of Areli underscores his role in the establishment of tribal divisions and clans that shaped Israel's identity and organization.
